checks: Use the correction procedure and how corroboration changes it to distinguish retaining a source from treating its claim as decisive. Independently blind-solved and checked against the English text, Traditional Chinese translation, rationale, distractors and sibling items.

activeQuestion.prompt: What distinction is the curator making when she says that the museum can make the label clearer “without giving it the last word”?
activeQuestion.promptZh: 策展人說可以把說明寫得更清楚，但「without giving it the last word」。她在區分哪兩件事？

options.text: Making the current explanation understandable versus treating it as a complete account that cannot be supplemented.
options.zh: 把目前的解說寫清楚，與把它當成不能再補充的完整說法。
options.whyZh: 可以讓人讀懂現有解說，同時保留未來補充新材料的空間；她接著指向訪客可留下補充資料的位置。

options.text: Describing the exhibit in writing versus letting teachers explain it orally at previews.
options.zh: 以文字介紹展品，與在預展時讓老師口頭解說。
options.whyZh: 老師提出的是改字樣的建議；策展人沒有區分文字與口述兩種展示方式。

options.text: Making an explanation understandable to children versus making it historically accurate for adults.
options.zh: 讓兒童看得懂解說，與讓成人看到符合史實的解說。
options.whyZh: 老師只說希望孩子更容易看懂；策展人的重點不是兒童和成人各用一套標準，也沒有說清楚和準確只能選一項。

options.text: Letting visitors add materials versus giving them the authority to replace the museum’s current account.
options.zh: 允許訪客補充資料，與交由訪客決定如何取代博物館目前的說法。
options.whyZh: 文章並未談到把改寫展覽的權力交給訪客。說明是否清楚、是否還能補充，才是這句話對照的重點。

activeQuestion.explanationZh: 策展人一方面想把目前的解說寫清楚，另一方面指向讓訪客補充資料的地方，表示解說並非最後定論。她沒有把決定權交給訪客，照片也還沒經過檢視。此處 giving it the last word 比喻把目前的說法視為定論。
activeQuestion.evidence: Paragraph 3’s metaphor is contextualized by the curator pointing to visitor notes and a prospective break-room photograph; paragraph 2 limits what can be treated as an established finding.

vocabulary.note: 此處把最後發言比喻為不再容許補充的最終說法。
加上尚未包含的資訊或材料。

group.title: What the Tin Was Called
group.passage:
From a fictional neighborhood museum’s exhibition blog

When the Hollybank Neighborhood Museum found a tin labeled “BOAT PINS” among items donated from the old ferry office, the first draft of its exhibition label described it as a container for spare parts. Former ferry clerk Ada Moore laughed when she read the draft. “We wrote ‘boat pins’ because anything marked ‘biscuits’ would have been gone before the evening crew arrived,” she said. The museum had an undated recording in which another worker mentioned sharing food on evening shifts, but the worker never identified the container.

Before opening, the curator set two rules. The exact wording on a donated object would appear as part of its display, even if visitors might mistake it for a literal description. And a firsthand recollection could appear beside an object, but it could be presented as the museum’s own finding only if a second independent source identified that same object and supported the specific claim being made.

At a preview, a teacher suggested replacing “BOAT PINS” on the display with “BISCUITS” so children would understand the story. The curator replied, “We can make the label clearer without giving it the last word.” She pointed to a space reserved for visitor notes: one family had already offered to bring in a photograph of the ferry staff break room.
group.passageZh:
以下是虛構的社區博物館展覽部落格文章。

霍利班克社區博物館在舊渡輪辦公室捐出的物品中找到一個寫著「BOAT PINS」（船用銷釘）的鐵盒。展覽說明牌的初稿將它描述為存放備用零件的容器。曾任渡輪站務員的艾達・摩爾讀了初稿，忍不住笑了。她說：「我們在盒上寫『船用銷釘』，因為只要寫上『餅乾』，還沒等晚班同事來上班，裡頭的東西就會被吃光。」博物館有一段未註明日期的錄音，另一名員工在錄音中提到大家會在晚班時分享食物，但未指認那個容器。

展覽開幕前，策展人訂了兩項規則。捐贈文物上的原文要在展出時呈現，即使參觀者可能按字面誤解也一樣。親歷者的回憶可以放在文物旁，但只有在第二個獨立來源能辨認出同一件文物，且能支持該項說法時，博物館才能把這項說法列為館方的研究結論。

在預展上，有位老師建議把展示中的「BOAT PINS」換成「BISCUITS」（餅乾），讓孩子更容易了解這段故事。策展人回答：「我們可以把說明寫清楚，但不必把它當作最後定論。」她指向留給訪客補充資料的地方：已經有一家人表示願意帶來一張渡輪員工休息室的照片。

originalQuestion.prompt: How should damaged stock be treated?

options.text: Combine it with undamaged stock in a single count
options.zh: 和未受損的庫存合併計數
options.whyZh: 公告要求受損庫存另行計數，不能和未受損庫存合計。
公告最後一句明確指定另行計數。

options.text: Automatically adjust its quantity to zero
options.whyZh: 任何調整前都要先查核差異，未授權直接歸零。

originalQuestion.explanationZh: 公告最後一句明確指定另行計數。
originalQuestion.evidence: Damaged stock must be counted separately rather than omitted.

vocabulary.note: 查明差異後修正系統中的庫存紀錄。
將庫存材料發給使用部門。
